title: Offset-mapped KV liveness + decode-wave throttling for paged attention
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem:
Current paged-attention KV allocator uses coarse page residency heuristics which leads to fragmented hot segments and occasional decode stalls under multi-tenant workloads. Prefill bursts can overwhelm decode throughput, causing 95th percentile token latency spikes and tail cost increases. Kernel selection does not account for fragment contiguity, so suboptimal kernels are chosen for fragmented spans, further increasing latency.

Goal:
Design and implement an "offset-mapped" KV binding layer that maintains compact liveness metadata per fragment (small metadata per page) and a decode-wave throttler that regulates prefill concurrency by sequence-offset alignment. Combine those with a kernel-affinity hinting API so the scheduler prefers kernels optimized for contiguous fragments. Primary goals: reduce 95th percentile token latency by 15% in mixed workloads, reduce memory amplification from fragmentation by 10-20%, and avoid decode-induced tail spikes during prefill-heavy traffic.

Approach:
1) Offset-mapped binding: maintain a lightweight mapping from logical KV offsets to physical page segments with a per-fragment liveness score (decays over time, boosted on hits). The mapping supports O(1) coalescing of adjacent live fragments for contiguous allocation.
2) Liveness-driven eviction: evict low-liveness fragments first across shards; incorporate an age+access score rather than pure LRU to avoid premature eviction of moderately-frequent small fragments. Provide a soft-reserve for hot prefixes to avoid churn during bursts.
3) Decode-wave throttler: introduce a scheduler that groups concurrent prefill requests into decode waves aligned by offset windows (configurable window size). Waves are admitted at a controlled rate to match decode throughput and avoid KV contention. When a wave completes, coalesce freed fragments aggressively to reduce fragmentation.
4) Kernel-affinity hints: expose a per-wave hint to the kernel selector indicating whether the wave targets contiguous fragments. The kernel selector will prefer contiguous-optimized kernels (faster memory paths) when appropriate; fallback remains unchanged.

Trade-offs considered:
- Memory overhead: storing per-fragment liveness adds ~6-12 bytes per fragment. Benchmarks suggest this overhead is offset by reduced fragmentation and fewer copies in the long tail for typical workloads.
- Latency vs. throughput: throttle aggressiveness affects throughput. Conservative defaults favor latency SLOs; allow customer-tunable policies for throughput-focused deployments (Dedicated).
- Complexity: adds a binding layer and new scheduler. Keep interfaces small and incremental: start with opt-in feature flag, then enable by rollout stages.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end integration tests exercising allocation, eviction, coalescing under synthetic workloads.
- Benchmark on stage cluster with mixed tenants: 95th token latency reduced >= 15% vs baseline; fragmentation metric (total free fragments / used pages) reduced >= 10%.
- No regression on median latency or throughput beyond 5% for base workloads.
- Kernel selector correctly picks contiguous kernels >= 80% of the time when wave hint is true.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag and per-tenant config.
- Canary rollout to internal tenants for 48h; collect prefill wave metrics, tail latency, and KV compaction rates.
- Gradual ramp to 10% traffic, then 50% over two days if metrics stable.

Monitoring & dashboards:
- New dashboards: wave_admit_rate, wave_queue_depth, fragment_liveness_dist, allocated_contiguity_ratio, kernel_affinity_hits.
- Alert: sustained wave_queue_depth > 500 for > 5m, or 95th token latency degradation > 10% vs baseline.

Open questions / blockers:
- Prefill window sizing: static vs adaptive. We will prototype static windows (64/128 token offsets) and evaluate adaptiveness later.
- Interaction with existing prefix caching heuristics (ENG-44789): need to ensure soft-reserve doesn't starve other tenants.
- Quantization/packed-kernel interactions: ensure kernel-affinity hints are compatible with quantized execution paths.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/offset-mapped-kv-binding
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2716
- Stage perf run: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/runtime/paged-attention/ENG-98114/2026-03-05
comments: 2026-02-11 — Initial triage: scoped as P1 after SRE reported repeated 95th spikes under multi-tenant synthetic prefill. Assigned to Marco for spike diagnosis.

2026-02-17 — Investigation update: found that fragmentation increases ~28% after sustained 30s prefill bursts; kernel selector fallback to generic kernels in 37% of decode windows. Recorded sample traces attached to Confluence doc.
2026-02-24 — Design review notes (from Priya Shah, PM): recommended adding a soft-reserve for hot prefixes to reduce oscillation; agreed to add config and clear metrics to observe impact.

2026-03-02 — Eng sync: implemented initial offset-mapped table and liveness decay logic. Microbenchmarks show coalescing reduces number of fragments by ~14% on synthetic mix. Prototype PR opened (see link in description).

2026-03-05 — Bench results on stage (run id in dashboards): 95th token latency improved 18% on mixed workloads with conservative throttle settings. However, throughput dropped ~4% for heavy-approximate embeddings workload. Decision: tune admit rate heuristics and run another pass.

2026-03-08 — Code review feedback (from Lin Wei): tighten locks around coalesce to avoid stall during global compaction; suggested optimistic coalescing and background compaction thread. Added TODO in PR.
2026-03-10 — Security review (not required): confirmed no plaintext secrets in mapping; access to liveness table limited to runtime process. Recorded note in ticket.

2026-03-12 — Current status: In Progress. Implemented decode-wave throttler prototype and kernel-affinity hint plumbing. Running extended stage soak to validate memory overhead and kernel selector behavior. Next: address Lin's locking suggestion and add canary rollout plan in console.
